subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: Self-Healing Concrete: Buildings That Repair Themselves
description: A micro-lesson that makes Self-Healing Concrete: Buildings That Repair Themselves usable.

hook.text: Dutch scientists put bacteria in concrete. When cracks form and water enters, bacteria wake up and produce limestone as sealant.

buildup.text: Concrete cracks are inevitable. Water enters, rusts the rebar, and weakens the structure. Repairs cost billions every year.

discovery.text: Bacillus bacteria survive dormant in concrete for 200 years. Water activates them to convert calcium into calcite — limestone.

twist.text: The bacteria can only heal cracks up to 0.8 mm wide. Major structural failures still need human repair — biology has limits.

climax.text: Field trials in the Netherlands and UK show promise. At scale, self-healing concrete could halve infrastructure maintenance costs.

punchline.text: Bacteria sleeping in concrete. Waiting for a crack. Then fixing it.

quiz.question: How do bacteria heal cracks in self-healing concrete?
options: They produce a sticky biofilm that glues the crack surfaces back together
They convert calcium into calcite limestone when activated by water entering cracks
They consume the cracked concrete and excrete a stronger polymer replacement
